The idea

Rooted in physics. Written for people.

Ryan Laird is an astrophysicist, science communicator and strategist working across space, sustainability and technology. The brand has to hold all three: rigorous enough for scientists, clear enough for everyone else, and calm enough to build trust.

  • 01

    Precise

    Claims are specific, sourced and checkable. Numbers carry units, and credentials are stated plainly.

  • 02

    Plain

    Short sentences, concrete nouns, and no jargon without a gloss. If a ten-second read doesn’t carry the point, the copy isn’t finished.

  • 03

    Curious

    Wonder is welcome. The identity borrows from orbits and instruments rather than stock galaxies and lens flares.

  • 04

    Accessible

    Contrast, structure and reduced-motion support are designed in, not retrofitted. WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor.

The logo system

One mark. Every scale.

An orbit mark and a two-tone wordmark, drawn as outlines so they hold up from a 16px favicon to a conference banner.

See logo rules and downloads →

Colour system

Dark sky. One clear signal.

Ink-first surfaces, warm white type and a single lead accent. Every pairing is contrast-tested, and the numbers are computed from the tokens.

  • Ink #0B0F1A
  • Warm White #EDEAE3
  • Teal #00C2A8
  • Amber #F5A623
  • Violet #A78BFA
  • Coral #FF8080
  • Green #4ADE80
  • Sky #38BDF8
